title: Early voting starts in New York, New Jersey elections; Mamdani casts ballot - ABC7 New York
text:
Early voting starts in New York, New Jersey elections; Mamdani casts ballot - ABC7 New York 
 24/7 Live New York City New Jersey Long Island Northern Suburbs Connecticut POLITICS 
 Early voting starts in New York and New Jersey 
 Brian Shlonsky has the latest details. Sunday, October 25, 2026 4:04AM Share Follow abc7NY on Google NEW YORK (WABC) -- Early voting began Saturday in New York and New Jersey, giving voters across the Tri-state area an opportunity to cast ballots ahead of Election Day.
 One of the top races is New York Governor.
 Sitting Governor Kathy Hochul and Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman campaigned on opposite sides of the state on Saturday.
 Crystal Cranmore has the details. 
 Blakeman was on Staten Island.
 "There's nobody here that could look your kid or your grandkid in the eye and honestly say you are going to have a better life in New York than I had Unless we change the governor of this state," he said.
 Governor Hochul was upstate in Buffalo.
 "Our message here is simple: I have a record of accomplishment over the last five years; I've delivered for all of New York," said Hochul.
 The most recent polls have Hochul squarely leading by double-digits.
 Hochul, backed by NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani -- who was cheered and also heckled as he headed in to cast his ballot a the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
 The mayor cast his ballot on Saturday morning at the Met. 
 He was asked what he thinks about the five ballot proposals and he said he "won't tell New Yorkers how to vote but I can tell you, as a New Yorker, I was proud to fill my ballot and vote yes on all five ballot proposals."
 Mamdani also said he is "looking forward to my governor getting reelected."

 Several polling places across New York city were busy until the 5 p.m. close, with lines out the door at the Natural History Museum on the Upper West Side.
 The nine days of early, in-person voting are in place to give voters flexibility and cut down on wait times on Election Day on Tuesday, November 3.
